Surgical repair is performed utilizing a two-patch technique (Dacron for inlet VSD and autologous pericardium for primum ASD) or a modified single-patch technique, dividing the bridging leaflets and suspending them onto the patch.

The left atrioventricular valve cleft is closed with interrupted non-absorbable sutures to achieve competence without causing mitral stenosis, and conduction tissue running along the crest of the ventricular septum is strictly avoided.
The elongated left ventricular outflow tract (goose-neck deformity on angiography) predisposes to subaortic stenosis in up to 5 to 10 percent of patients following surgical repair.

modules.name: Ebstein Anomaly: Pathoanatomy, Delamination and the Cone Reconstruction Technique

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 113 (Ebstein Anomaly of the Tricuspid Valve)

mustKnow.fact: Ebstein anomaly is characterized by failure of delamination of the tricuspid valve leaflets from the underlying myocardium, leading to downward apical displacement of the septal and posterior leaflets into the right ventricle.

Apical displacement divides the right ventricle into a proximal thinned atrialized right ventricle that contracts paradoxically with the right atrium, and a small, functionally compromised true functional right ventricle.

The anterior tricuspid leaflet is characteristically sail-like and redundant, remaining attached at the true annular level, while the septal and posterior leaflets are hypoplastic, tethered, or absent.

Accessory conduction pathways (Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome) occur in 20 to 30 percent of patients with Ebstein anomaly, predominantly right-sided posteroseptal or posterolateral accessory bypass tracts causing supraventricular tachycardias.

The Great Ormond Street Hospital (Carpentier) echocardiographic severity score compares the combined area of the right atrium and atrialized RV to that of the functional RV and left heart, with a ratio greater than 1.5 indicating severe disease.

The cone reconstruction technique (da Silva procedure) is the modern gold standard surgical repair, extensively mobilizing and delaminating all tethered tricuspid leaflet tissue from the RV wall and septum.

The mobilized leaflets are rotated and sutured edge-to-edge to form a 360-degree circumferential cone of valve tissue, re-anchored to the true anatomical tricuspid annulus combined with annuloplasty ring stabilization and atrialized RV plication.

In patients with severe right ventricular dysfunction incapable of maintaining full cardiac output, a bidirectional cavopulmonary shunt (one-and-a-half ventricle repair) is added to unload the compromised right ventricle.

modules.name: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: 8th TNM Staging, Lobectomy, Sleeve and Segmentectomy

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Lung cancer; Current Lung Cancer 8th Edition Staging System; Treatments for Lung Cancer)

mustKnow.fact: In the 8th Edition IASLC/AJCC TNM staging for lung cancer, T1 is 3 cm or less, T2 is greater than 3 cm up to 5 cm, T3 is greater than 5 cm up to 7 cm (or invading chest wall, pericardium, or separate same-lobe nodule), and T4 is greater than 7 cm or invading mediastinum, heart, great vessels, or carina.

Nodal staging defines N1 as ipsilateral peribronchial, interlobar, or hilar lymph nodes; N2 as ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal nodes; and N3 as contralateral mediastinal, contralateral hilar, or supraclavicular nodes.

Preoperative cardiopulmonary risk assessment requires spirometry and diffusion capacity (DLCO), where predicted postoperative FEV1 and DLCO exceeding 40 percent indicate low risk for major anatomic lung resection.

Anatomic lobectomy with systematic mediastinal lymph node dissection (minimum 3 mediastinal stations including station 7 subcarinal and 3 N1 stations) remains the standard of care for resectable stage I and II non-small cell lung cancer.

The CALGB 140503 and JCOG0802 randomized trials established that sublobar anatomic segmentectomy achieves non-inferior overall survival and recurrence rates compared to lobectomy for peripheral stage IA NSCLC tumors 2 cm or smaller.

Bronchial sleeve lobectomy is preferred over pneumonectomy for centrally located tumors invading the mainstem bronchus, preserving pulmonary parenchymal function and conferring superior operative survival and long-term quality of life.

Minimally invasive approaches (video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery or robotic-assisted thoracic surgery) yield equivalent oncologic survival with significantly reduced postoperative pain, shorter hospital stay, and lower pulmonary complications.

In patients with resectable Stage IIIA (N2) disease, induction neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (such as platinum doublet plus nivolumab based on the CheckMate 816 trial) followed by surgical resection achieves high pathological complete response and prolonged event-free survival.

modules.name: Mediastinal Masses: Anatomical Compartments, Diagnostic Workup and Surgical Approach

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Mediastinum; Primary Mediastinal Neoplasms)

mustKnow.fact: The mediastinum is anatomically divided into the anterosuperior (prevascular), middle (visceral), and posterior (paravertebral sulci) compartments, each characterized by distinct resident structures and classic pathological masses.

The 4 Ts rule defines the common anterior mediastinal masses: Thymoma (and thymic carcinoma), Teratoma (and germ cell tumors), Thyroid (retrosternal goiter), and Terrible lymphoma (Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma).
The middle mediastinum contains pericardial cysts, bronchogenic cysts, enteric duplication cysts, lymphadenopathy, and vascular aneurysms, bordered by the pericardium and tracheal bifurcation.

The posterior mediastinum (paravertebral gutter) is predominantly the site of neurogenic tumors arising from peripheral nerves (schwannoma, neurofibroma) or the sympathetic chain (ganglioneuroma, neuroblastoma).

Serum biomarkers are mandatory in every patient with an anterior mediastinal mass before invasive biopsy: elevated alpha-fetoprotein confirms non-seminomatous germ cell tumor, while beta-hCG is elevated in choriocarcinoma, embryonal, and some seminomas.

Pure seminoma presents with elevated beta-hCG in 10 percent of cases, but alpha-fetoprotein is strictly normal; any elevation in AFP establishes the presence of a non-seminomatous component requiring upfront platinum-based chemotherapy.

Posterior neurogenic tumors with intraspinal canal extension (dumbbell or hourglass tumors) require contrast MRI of the spine and a coordinated single-stage combined neurosurgical laminectomy and thoracic surgical excision.

In patients with large anterior mediastinal masses producing critical tracheobronchial or superior vena caval compression, general anesthesia with positive pressure ventilation risks catastrophic airway collapse and death, requiring awake fiberoptic intubation or ECMO standby.

modules.name: Thymoma and Myasthenia Gravis: Masaoka Staging, Extended Thymectomy and VATS

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Primary Mediastinal Neoplasms; Thymoma)

mustKnow.fact: Thymoma is the most common primary neoplasm of the anterior mediastinum, associated with autoimmune myasthenia gravis in 30 to 50 percent of cases and pure red cell aplasia or hypogammaglobulinemia (Good syndrome) in 5 percent.
Approximately 10 to 15 percent of all patients presenting with myasthenia gravis harbor an underlying thymoma on contrast-enhanced chest CT.

The Masaoka-Koga staging system classifies thymoma into Stage I (macroscopically completely encapsulated with no microscopic capsular invasion), Stage II (microscopic capsular invasion or macroscopic invasion into surrounding mediastinal fat or pleura), Stage III (macroscopic invasion into neighbouring organs such as pericardium, great vessels, or lung), and Stage IV (pleural/pericardial dissemination or distant metastases).

The WHO histologic classification categorizes thymic epithelial tumors into Type A, AB, B1, B2, and B3 based on the ratio of neoplastic epithelial cells to non-neoplastic lymphocytes, and thymic carcinoma (Type C) which exhibits overt cytological malignancy.

Extended total thymectomy is the mandatory surgical standard of care, requiring complete en bloc resection of the entire thymus gland (both upper cervical poles) along with all anterior mediastinal, pericardiophrenic, and cervical fatty tissue from phrenic nerve to phrenic nerve.

The MGTX randomized trial proved that in non-thymomatous acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis, extended transsternal thymectomy significantly improves clinical symptoms, lowers quantitative myasthenia scores, and reduces prednisone requirements.

Minimally invasive thymectomy (VATS or robotic-assisted thymectomy) achieves complete R0 resection rates and neurological remission equivalent to open median sternotomy for Stage I and II thymomas with significantly less blood loss and shorter hospital stay.

Adjuvant mediastinal radiation therapy is indicated following complete surgical resection for Masaoka Stage II with extensive capsular invasion or Stage III thymomas to reduce local pleural recurrence.

modules.name: Pleural Infection: Light Criteria, Parapneumonic Effusion Stages and Thoracoscopic Decortication

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Pleura; Empyema)

mustKnow.fact: Light criteria classify pleural fluid as an exudate if pleural fluid to serum protein ratio exceeds 0.5, pleural fluid to serum LDH ratio exceeds 0.6, or pleural fluid LDH exceeds two-thirds the upper limit of normal serum LDH.

Parapneumonic effusions evolve across three distinct stages: Stage 1 (exudative, sterile free-flowing fluid), Stage 2 (fibropurulent, dense fibrin deposition, loculations, bacterial invasion), and Stage 3 (organizing, thick collagenous pleural peel trapping the lung).

A complicated parapneumonic effusion requiring mandatory tube thoracostomy drainage is defined by pleural fluid pH below 7.20, glucose below 40 to 60 mg/dL, LDH greater than 1000 IU/L, or positive Gram stain or culture.

Overt empyema is established by the macroscopic presence of frank pus in the pleural cavity, which never resolves with systemic antibiotics alone and mandates immediate complete mechanical evacuation.

Intrapleural fibrinolytic and enzyme therapy combining tissue plasminogen activator (tPA, 10 mg) and human recombinant deoxyribonuclease (DNase, 5 mg) administered twice daily for 3 days significantly improves fluid drainage and reduces surgical referral in loculated effusions (MIST-2 trial).

Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) debridement and decortication is the surgical procedure of choice for Stage 2 multiloculated empyema failing tube drainage, breaking loculations and evacuating gelatinous fibrin peels.

In chronic Stage 3 organizing empyema with a thick fibroblastic peel incarcerating the lung parenchyma, open thoracotomy decortication is required to peel away the visceral cortex and allow full pulmonary re-expansion.

Postpneumonectomy empyema with bronchopleural fistula is managed emergently with pleural drainage, followed by open pleural window thoracostomy (Eloesser flap or Clagett procedure) and delayed cavity obliteration with antibiotic solution or muscle transposition.

modules.name: Spontaneous Pneumothorax: Apical Blebs, Bullectomy and Mechanical Pleurodesis

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Pleura; Pneumothorax)

mustKnow.fact: Primary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs in tall, thin young individuals (typically 15 to 35 years old) without underlying clinical lung disease, caused by the rupture of subpleural apical blebs or bullae.

Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax occurs as a complication of underlying parenchymal lung disease, most commonly chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with emphysema, cystic fibrosis, or necrotizing pneumonia.

Tension pneumothorax develops via a one-way valve mechanism where air enters the pleural space during inspiration but cannot exit during expiration, generating positive intrapleural pressure that causes mediastinal shift, caval compression, and obstructive shock.

Emergency decompression of tension pneumothorax requires immediate needle thoracostomy with a large-bore (14-gauge) catheter in the second intercostal space midclavicular line or fourth/fifth intercostal space anterior axillary line, followed immediately by tube thoracostomy.

Indications for surgical intervention in primary spontaneous pneumothorax include second ipsilateral episode (first recurrence), first contralateral episode, bilateral synchronous pneumothorax, persistent air leak exceeding 3 to 5 days, or high-risk professions (pilots, deep-sea divers).

Thoracoscopic bullectomy (VATS) utilizing endoscopic surgical staplers resects apical subpleural blebs and bullae, inspecting both the apex of the upper lobe and the superior segment of the lower lobe.

Concomitant mechanical pleurodesis (pleural abrasion using dry gauze or Marlex mesh) or apical parietal pleurectomy is performed to induce dense sterile fibroblastic symphysis and reduce late recurrence to under 2 to 5 percent.

Chemical pleurodesis utilizing sterile talc poudrage (via thoracoscopy) or talc slurry (via chest tube) generates intense pleural inflammation, reserved predominantly for secondary pneumothorax or patients unfit for definitive surgical resection.

modules.name: Tracheal Stenosis and Tumours: Diagnostic Workup, Resection and End-to-End Anastomosis

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Trachea; Benign Stenosis of the Trachea; Principles of Tracheal Surgery)

mustKnow.fact: Post-intubation and post-tracheostomy tracheal stenosis is caused by high endotracheal tube cuff pressures exceeding mucosal capillary perfusion pressure (20 to 30 mmHg), leading to circumferential mucosal ischemia, necrosis, ulceration, and dense fibrotic cicatrization.

Clinical stridor and exertional dyspnea typically develop several weeks to months following extubation once the internal tracheal luminal diameter is reduced below 5 to 6 mm (or greater than 50 percent cross-sectional reduction).

Dynamic high-resolution computed tomography of the airway combined with flexible and rigid bronchoscopy provides precise anatomical measurement of stenotic length, distance from the vocal cords, and distance to the carina.

The safe limit for primary circumferential tracheal resection with direct end-to-end anastomosis is up to 4 to 5 centimetres (approximately 5 to 7 tracheal rings, or nearly 50 percent of total tracheal length in young flexible adults).

Laryngeal release maneuvers (suprahyoid Montgomery release or thyrohyoid Dedo release) provide an additional 1 to 2 cm of proximal tracheal mobility to relieve anastomotic tension without compromising deglutition.
Right hilar mobilization, division of the inferior pulmonary ligament, and intrapericardial release of the right pulmonary veins provide 2 to 3 cm of distal tracheal and carinal upward mobility.

Anastomotic reconstruction is performed using interrupted 4-0 polyglactin or polydioxanone absorbable sutures with knots tied externally, maintaining cervical neck flexion postoperatively with a guardian chin-to-chest stitch for 7 days.

Primary tracheal neoplasms are rare, predominantly comprising adenoid cystic carcinoma (slow-growing, marked propensity for perineural invasion, high radiosensitivity) and squamous cell carcinoma (ulcerating, smoking-related, early nodal metastases).

modules.name: Chest Wall Deformities: Pectus Excavatum, Nuss Procedure and Modified Ravitch Repair

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Chest Wall; Congenital Deformities)

mustKnow.fact: Pectus excavatum (funnel chest) is the most common congenital chest wall deformity, characterized by posterior depression of the sternum and lower costal cartilages, occurring with a male-to-female ratio of 4 to 1.

The Haller index (pectus severity index) on non-contrast chest CT is calculated by dividing the transverse inner diameter of the chest by the anterior-posterior distance between the posterior sternum and anterior spine.

A Haller index greater than 3.25 defines severe pectus excavatum deformity and represents a standard objective criterion for surgical repair reimbursement and intervention (normal Haller index is approximately 2.5).
Severe depression causes right ventricular compression, reduced right ventricular stroke volume, and decreased exercise tolerance with restrictive pulmonary impairment.

The minimally invasive Nuss procedure inserts one or two custom-bent concave steel or titanium bars retrosternally under bilateral thoracoscopic guidance, rotating the bar 180 degrees to instantly elevate the sternum without cartilage resection.
The pectus bar is secured with lateral stabilizing plates and pericostal wire fixations, remaining in place for 2 to 3 years before elective removal once permanent chest wall remodeling is mature.

The open modified Ravitch repair involves subperichondrial resection of all deformed costal cartilages, transverse sternal wedge osteotomy, and sternal stabilization using an anterior support strut or plate.

Pectus carinatum (pigeon chest) is protrusion of the sternum, managed initially with external dynamic chest compression bracing in compliant skeletally immature adolescents, or modified Ravitch chondrosternoplasty if rigid or refractory.

modules.name: Bronchiectasis, Aspergilloma and Lung Abscess: Indications and Surgical Resection

topics.book: Sabiston Surgery 22e Ch 110 (Pulmonary Infections; Bronchiectasis; Lung Abscess; Fungal Infections)

mustKnow.fact: Bronchiectasis is irreversible, abnormal bronchial dilatation resulting from a vicious cycle of transmural infection and inflammation, presenting with copious purulent sputum, chronic cough, and recurrent massive hemoptysis.

High-resolution computed tomography is the gold standard imaging diagnostic modality, demonstrating the signet ring sign (internal bronchial diameter exceeding adjacent pulmonary arterial diameter) and lack of peripheral bronchial tapering.

Surgical resection (anatomic lobectomy or segmentectomy) is indicated for localized, focal bronchiectasis failing medical therapy, or for life-threatening hemoptysis refractory to bronchial artery embolization.
Complete surgical extirpation of all diseased dilated segments with healthy margins is critical, as residual diseased tissue leads to high rates of recurrent postoperative suppuration.

Simple aspergilloma (mycetoma or fungal ball) develops in pre-existing cavitary lung lesions (most commonly old tuberculosis cavities), manifesting radiographically with the Monod or air crescent sign.

Surgical resection is the definitive treatment of choice for pulmonary aspergilloma associated with hemoptysis, requiring careful dissection to avoid intraoperative rupture and fungal spillage into the pleural cavity.

Primary lung abscesses are predominantly caused by aspiration of anaerobic oral commensal flora in patients with impaired consciousness, resolving with prolonged targeted antibiotic therapy in greater than 85 to 90 percent of cases.

Surgical resection (lobectomy) for lung abscess is reserved for failure of medical therapy after 4 to 6 weeks, large thick-walled cavity exceeding 4 to 6 cm refractory to drainage, suspected underlying malignancy, or life-threatening hemorrhage.
